change.title: Durabilize non-one-click destructive mutation receipts
change.summary: Implements the bounded P2-B source slice for mode, settings, applied-profile revoke, Codex authentication, and Codex network mutations. The Desktop now uses one credential-free config-mutation-operation.v1 receipt with a sibling exact Config fence, exact Pending-to-InProgress attempt checkpoints before every real effect, terminal clearing tombstone, and fail-closed boot/admission recovery; intent-only profile surfaces return exact typed outcomes without claiming a receipt. Codex auth sidecars stay inert until exact identity is durable and a flushed start acknowledgement linearizes authorization. P2-A, one-click/history journals, credentials, real providers, installed artifacts, signing, and release remain separate evidence boundaries.

basis: exact P2-A source candidate 09cbc686c61228eba592475dec6e9e327658b4a2 is the frozen implementation base
receipt and Config-fence tests cover bounded no-clobber CAS, clearing resurrection, orphan/receipt-only recovery, and admission blocking for ordinary writers, P2-A, and every one-click effect route

every real runtime, Config, auth, profile, and SSH effect exact-CASes Pending to InProgress with a fresh attempt identity before execution, then CASes a bounded terminal outcome or retains typed attention
auth start tests serialize the bounded start write against supervisor cancel and native exit, flush start_ack before Gateway authorization, then preserve the post-start cancel channel

auth stream tests reap protocol errors, persist exact in-progress identity for login and logout, require exact signal identity for each sidecar, and reject logout success without an exact logged-out generation
Codex network UI accepts only receipt-free exact committed intents for non-destructive writes or operation-id-bound exact completed terminal receipts for destructive writes
mode-switch UI accepts only the exact set_mode intent outcome or the exact destructive set_mode_official terminal outcome before publishing the selected mode

settings and profile UI consumers distinguish exact intents from destructive terminal outcomes; applied revocation completes its separate rolling-backup effect only after unlink, directory fsync, and absence proof
Codex login success, failure, cancellation, protocol-error, and logout terminal receipts derive stopped versus preserved runtime state from the actual fenced preflight action

auth failure-seam tests cover reservation release, terminal PID clearing, dynamic after-image drift, logout in-progress identity, terminal mutation-ID binding, generation references, and dual-receipt boot conflict

frontend and preview tests bind durable terminal identity, validate active-profile aliases and repeated no-change selection, require exact logout mutation/generation/warning fields, and reject malformed responses
no artifact, installed App, live provider, live Science, credentials, signing, notarization, or public release evidence is claimed
